name: Advanced Diploma in Theology and Ministry
Bachelor of Counselling
description:
The Bachelor of Counselling sits a little apart from the rest of the University of Divinity's catalogue, which is otherwise almost entirely theology and ministry. This is a professional counselling degree, though it's taught within a university whose identity and college network are explicitly Christian, and several of its member colleges (Whitley College, Eastern College Australia among them) fold a pastoral or values-based counselling orientation into the training rather than treating it as incidental.

Students complete core counselling theory, ethics and practice units alongside supervised placement hours, working toward eligibility for professional counselling registration in Australia (typically ACA or PACFA-aligned pathways depending on the specific college and cohort). The counselling degree exists partly because chaplaincy, pastoral care and church-based welfare work are common destinations for University of Divinity graduates broadly, and a dedicated counselling qualification lets students formalise that pastoral instinct into a registrable clinical skill set.

Graduates go into private practice, community and church-based counselling services, and pastoral care roles in hospitals, schools and aged care, often building on a values framework that's more explicit here than in a secular counselling degree elsewhere.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Counselling Theory, Human Development, Communication Skills, Ethics in Counselling
Year 2: Counselling Practice and Techniques, Family and Relationship Counselling, Trauma-Informed Practice, supervised placement I
Year 3: Group Work and Facilitation, Counselling in Faith and Community Contexts, advanced supervised placement, capstone case study portfolio

name: Bachelor of Ministry
description:
The Bachelor of Ministry is the more vocationally focused sibling of the Bachelor of Theology: same three-year, four-field structure (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry), but weighted harder toward the Mission and Ministry strand and toward practical placement, aimed squarely at students heading into lay ministry, youth or community ministry, or pastoral leadership roles that don't require the extended academic and language training built into a Master of Divinity.

Students complete it through one of the University of Divinity's member colleges, and many are already working in a church or parachurch role while studying part-time, which the degree structure accommodates: it can stretch to nine years part-time, the same maximum as the Bachelor of Theology.

It functions as a practical entry point into vocational ministry for people who know their calling is hands-on pastoral and community work rather than academic theology, without foreclosing the option of moving on to a Master of Divinity or Master of Theology later.
curriculum:
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Foundations of Christian Ministry, Humanities elective
Year 2: Pastoral Care and Ministry Practice, Christian Thought and History unit, supervised ministry placement I
Year 3: Leadership in Ministry Contexts, advanced Mission and Ministry electives, capstone ministry placement and reflective portfolio
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); typically undertaken alongside a church/ministry placement

name: Bachelor of Theology
description:
The Bachelor of Theology is the University of Divinity's foundational undergraduate degree, but "the university" here is a loose word for what's actually a federation: students enrol through one of the constituent colleges (Catholic Theological College, Pilgrim Theological College, Ridley College, Whitley College and others spanning Anglican, Baptist, Catholic, Lutheran, Uniting Church and Salvation Army traditions) rather than a single central campus, and take classes structured around four fields: Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Theology: Mission and Ministry.

That federated structure is the actual selling point, not a bureaucratic quirk. A Bachelor of Theology student can end up studying alongside seminarians from a different denomination entirely, taught by faculty formed in a different tradition, in a way that a single-denomination bible college simply can't replicate. The university has described itself as one of the more sustained ecumenical experiments in Australian higher education, going back over a century to its 1910 founding as the Melbourne College of Divinity.

The three-year, full-time degree suits people heading toward ministry, chaplaincy, religious education or further postgraduate theological study, and it can be completed over as long as nine years part-time, which matters given how many students are already working in parish or pastoral roles while they study.
curriculum:
Field of study across the degree: Biblical Studies (Old and New Testament units), Christian Thought and History (patristics through to modern theology), Theology: Mission and Ministry, Humanities electives
Year 1: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, foundational Humanities unit
Year 2: further Biblical Studies units, Church History, Ethics, a Mission and Ministry practicum unit
Year 3: advanced electives across the four fields, capstone unit chosen in consultation with the student's college

name: Diploma in Theology
description:
The Diploma in Theology is the University of Divinity's entry-level credential, shorter than the three-year bachelor degrees and pitched at students testing whether formal theological study suits them, those wanting a foundational qualification for a church or parachurch role without a full degree commitment, or students planning to build credit toward a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry later; completed units typically count toward the bachelor's degree if a student decides to continue.

It draws on the same four-field structure as the university's bachelor degrees (Humanities, Biblical Studies, Christian Thought and History, and Mission and Ministry), just compressed into a shorter, more introductory sequence, and like the rest of the university's offerings it's delivered through one of the constituent colleges rather than a single central faculty.

Graduates commonly move into entry-level church ministry support roles, or use the diploma as a stepping stone into a full bachelor's program once they've confirmed the direction suits them.
curriculum: Introduction to Old Testament, Introduction to New Testament, Introduction to Christian Thought, Foundations of Christian Ministry, one Humanities elective, one further elective chosen from Biblical Studies or Mission and Ministry
admission_requirements: Completion of Year 12 (or equivalent); no prior theological study required

name: Doctor of Philosophy (Theology)
description:
The Doctor of Philosophy (Theology) is the University of Divinity's highest research degree and, unlike the coursework-heavy Master of Divinity, it's almost entirely independent research: a substantial thesis supervised by a scholar drawn from one of the constituent colleges, examined externally in the standard Australian PhD model. Candidates work across the university's full theological range: biblical studies, systematic and historical theology, ethics, liturgical studies and practical theology, and supervision is matched to a candidate's specific research question rather than assigned by a single central department, since expertise is distributed across the college network.

What makes doctoral study here distinctive is the ecumenical breadth of supervisory expertise available under one doctoral framework: a candidate researching, say, Catholic sacramental theology and one researching Uniting Church ecclesiology can both be supervised and examined within the same PhD program, drawing on faculty across traditions the university has spent over a century bringing together.

Graduates go into academic theology, senior denominational leadership, and specialist research and teaching roles at seminaries and universities, both in Australia and internationally.
curriculum: Candidature milestones rather than semester units: confirmation of candidature (research proposal and literature review, typically within the first year), annual progress review, thesis writing across candidature (nominally three to four years full-time, longer part-time), final thesis submission and oral or written examination by external examiners
admission_requirements: Master's degree with a strong research component (Honours or equivalent); admission by School of Graduate Research Committee

name: Graduate Diploma in Divinity
description:
The Graduate Diploma in Divinity is a shorter postgraduate credential for students who already hold a bachelor's degree, often but not always in theology, and want structured graduate-level theological formation without committing to the full length of a Master of Divinity. It's a common pathway for people converting a degree in an unrelated field into theological qualification ahead of ministry candidacy, or for graduates of a Bachelor of Theology or Bachelor of Ministry wanting to add a postgraduate credential before deciding whether to pursue the full Master of Divinity.

Like everything else at the University of Divinity, it's delivered through a specific member college, so the exact mix of units, and how much practical ministry formation is built in versus purely academic content, depends on which college a student enrols with, whether that's a Catholic, Anglican, Uniting Church, Baptist or other tradition-specific institution within the federation.

Many students use it as a stepping stone: credit typically transfers into the Master of Divinity for those who go on to complete it, so the diploma isn't a dead end so much as a shorter first commitment.
curriculum: Core postgraduate units in Biblical Studies and Systematic Theology, Church History, an introductory Pastoral Ministry unit, electives chosen according to the student's college and intended pathway (often credit-bearing toward the Master of Divinity)

name: Master of Divinity
description:
The Master of Divinity is the professional ministry-formation degree at the University of Divinity, and its scale reflects that: 432 points across 18 units, a three-year full-time load that most students actually take considerably longer than three years to finish, since it's the standard qualifying degree for ordained ministry across several of the denominations that make up the university's college federation. It combines academic theological study (biblical languages, systematics, church history) with practical formation units in preaching, pastoral care, liturgy and mission that a purely academic theology degree wouldn't include.

Because students enrol through a specific college rather than a generic university faculty, the Master of Divinity looks noticeably different depending on whether it's taken at, say, a Catholic seminary college or a Baptist or Uniting Church college: denominational formation requirements, placement structures and even which biblical languages are compulsory can vary, even though the degree title and the awarding university are the same.

Graduates are typically heading toward ordination, chaplaincy or vocational ministry leadership, and the degree is usually a prerequisite step in a denomination's own candidacy and formation process rather than a stand-alone academic credential.
curriculum:
Year 1: Biblical Languages (Greek and/or Hebrew), Old and New Testament Studies, Introduction to Systematic Theology, Foundations of Pastoral Ministry
Year 2: Church History, Christian Ethics, Homiletics and Preaching, supervised field education placement
Year 3: Advanced Systematic Theology, Liturgy and Sacramental Theology, Mission and Ministry Practicum, integrative capstone unit tied to denominational formation requirements
admission_requirements: Bachelor's degree (any discipline); designed as professional preparation for ministry

name: Master of Theology
description:
The Master of Theology is the university's two-year (240-point, ten-unit) postgraduate research-leaning degree, sitting a level above coursework masters like the Master of Divinity in the amount of independent scholarly work it asks for. Students take it through one of the University of Divinity's member colleges, and the choice of college matters more than it would at a conventional university, since each carries its own denominational library, faculty specialisation and theological emphasis. A student drawn to Catholic sacramental theology and one drawn to Reformed biblical hermeneutics will often end up doing genuinely different degrees under the same university name.

The course typically combines advanced coursework units with a substantial research component, often a minor thesis, and it's commonly taken by clergy and religious professionals seeking to deepen expertise in a specific area: biblical languages, systematic theology, church history, rather than a general theological education, which the Bachelor of Theology or Master of Divinity already cover.

Graduates go on to doctoral study, teaching roles in theological colleges, or senior ministry and denominational leadership positions where advanced theological training is expected.
curriculum:
Year 1: advanced coursework units in the student's chosen specialisation (e.g. Biblical Studies, Systematic Theology, Church History), research methods unit
Year 2: further specialised coursework, minor thesis or major research project, oral presentation of research to college faculty
admission_requirements: A Bachelor of Theology, Bachelor of Ministry, or Master of Divinity specifically (a Graduate Certificate or Graduate Diploma alone is explicitly insufficient); or enrolment in a BTheol/BMin at University of Divinity with at least 378 points completed, provided it is finished within 12 months of admission to the Master of Theology. Probationary admission is not available.
english_requirements: English language proficiency is required per University of Divinity's Admissions Policy (Section 6), which applies to all coursework and HDR applicants, but the specific IELTS/TOEFL/PTE minimum scores are set out only in that policy document (not published on the course page itself), so a specific number cannot be confirmed from public program pages.
